conventions: A σύν-compound's associative English phrase goes to the expressed dative where the Greek writes one, and rides inside the compound's own unit where it does not. συνετάφημεν … αὐτῷ → We were buried … with him (6:4) and συζήσομεν … αὐτῷ → we shall … live with him (6:8) give with him to αὐτῷ under rule 106's oblique arm, the ASV writing buried and live for the verbs themselves; συνεσταυρώθη → was crucified with him* (6:6) keeps the whole supplied phrase inside the verb's unit headed on crucified, no dative standing to answer to the preverb. The same holds for a compound that is not a verb: the adjective σύμφυτοι → united with him* (6:5) keeps its supplied pronoun as a rule 7 helper headed on united, rule 106's test being whether another source token stands to answer to the word, not whether the compound is verbal.

In the formula χάρις … τῷ θεῷ → thanks be to God (6:17) the supplied copula goes to the dative and not to the subject. χάρις is a lexical noun, so rule 53's subject-carrier exception is switched off by rule 63, and rule 56 does not reach the clause because τῷ θεῷ stands in it. θεῷ takes be to God headed on God, its article unrepresented and the case preposition riding with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, as 2CO.8.16 and 2CO.9.15 read the identical formula. Reading the dative as a benefactive adjunct, so that the clause has no predicate at all and thanks be forms one unit, remains defensible; that was the earlier reading here.

Where the ASV writes a preposition's English twice — once as a separate word before the antecedent and once fused into a where- relative — the pair does not join under rule 35, rule 94's single-English-word precondition failing. The preposition takes its own word, the portmanteau is the relative's own unit whole, and the repeated element inside it is a rule 7 helper on the relative under rule 103's function-word arm rather than added. εἰς … ὃν … παρεδόθητε → to that form of teaching whereunto ye were delivered (6:17) gives to to εἰς and whereunto to ὅν, as ἐφ᾽ οἷς → in the things whereof (6:21) gives in to ἐπί and the things whereof to οἷς, headed on the nominal under rule 77.

κυριεύω → have dominion over heads on dominion under rule 91, the corpus spending the noun and not the light verb have on that lexeme, and the over goes to the governed genitive as the case government the verb expresses: κυριεύσει … ὑμῶν → shall not have dominion over you (6:14) and κυριεύει … αὐτοῦ → hath dominion over him (6:9) give over you and over him to the pronoun, as the corpus's five over you units head on the pronoun. Reading over as licensed by the frame's own noun dominion, so that it stays inside the verb's unit under rule 21's support-frame clause and the genitive keeps a bare pronoun, remains defensible; that clause's own examples all govern accusatives, where no case stands for an English preposition to realize.
report: Read all 35 candidate lemma groups and then the whole dump end to end for the splits the table cannot see (added-versus-fold decisions carry no source token). No genuine cross-verse split found; patches empty.

Candidates resolved as licensed by the source or by the ASV's own wording: οὕτως…καί at 6:4 (so / also) against 6:11 (Even so / also) is rule 100 with and without a written even; ὥσπερ as like as (6:4) against as (6:19) is the ASV's wording; the ὁ groups are the two arms of rule 20, which 6:5 writes in one verse — τοῦ emptied because αὐτοῦ stands, τῆς taking the supplied his because no possessor token does; ὅς heads on the relativizer at 6:2 and 6:16 (bare antecedent) and on the supplied nominal at 6:10 and 6:21, which is rule 77's own test and not two analyses; the articular infinitives at 6:6 and 6:12 differ only in whether a preposition governs the construction (rule 61).

Checked the four σύν-compounds together: 6:4 συνετάφημεν and 6:8 συζήσομεν give with him to the expressed dative αὐτῷ, while 6:6 συνεσταυρώθη and 6:5 σύμφυτοι keep the supplied italic with him* inside their own units because no dative stands. That is one analysis in two configurations, on rule 106's own no-other-source-token test. Logged as a convention because rule 106 is written for compound verbs and 6:5 is an adjective.

Checked the doubly realized prepositions at 6:17 (εἰς as to plus the -unto of whereunto) and 6:21 (ἐπί as in plus the -of of whereof). Both split the same way: the preposition takes its own word, the portmanteau stays whole on the relative, and the repeated element is a rule 7 helper under rule 103's function-word arm rather than added. Rule 35 does not join the pair, rule 94's single-English-word precondition failing. Logged.

Checked the supplied copulas: 6:17 (be to God), 6:21 (is death) and both clauses of 6:23 put the copula on the predicate because the subject is a lexical noun (rule 63); 6:22 supplies none. The two corrections already carried in verses/17.json — the copula moved from χάρις to θεῷ, and the second δέ aligned to whereas instead of added — are consistent with the rest of the chapter and with 2CO.8.16, 2CO.9.15 and 1CO.12.24 respectively. No δέ anywhere in the chapter is left unrepresented.

BSB: all ten disagreements are the documented convention difference and none is an error. Seven are articles emptied under rule 20 because a possessive already occupies the determiner slot (6:5 τοῦ, the four τά before members at 6:13 and 6:19, 6:19 τῆς before σαρκός, 6:22 τόν before καρπόν); two are articles the ASV gives no determiner at all (6:12 ἡ, and 6:19 τῇ, which keeps its to on the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause); and 6:5 ἀλλά is empty because the ASV writes no but for it, only the also of καί. Nothing was changed to move the rate.

Open edge left as accepted and logged rather than patched: κυριεύω + genitive at 6:9 and 6:14 puts over on the governed pronoun. Rule 21's support-frame clause could instead keep over inside the verb with dominion, and its own examples all govern accusatives, so the case is unsettled; but the two verses agree and the corpus's five over you units head on the pronoun, so a self-consistent pair is not worth breaking. The competing reading is named in the convention.

The validation report's 44 repeated notes are overwhelmingly restatements of rules 19, 21, 23 and 26 (Noun to noun, Preposition to preposition, Article → the). Those bind every verse already; logging them would bury the four judgments a later reader could not rederive, which are the ones recorded.
